prerequisites: Theory of Structures (or the Theory of Structures course from the first semester of the Master's)
Equilibrium, statics, centers of gravity, static moments, moments of inertia
Stress, deformation, stress-strain relationship, tension, shear, bending, torsion, buckling, isostatic and hyperstatic systems, stiffness
Pin-jointed bar structures (trusses), rigid-jointed bar structures, principle of virtual work, isostaticity and hyperstaticity, displaceability, stiffness, matrix calculation of bar structures

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving capacity in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Project, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Engineer profession.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation and design of structures.
Design and calculate pin-jointed and rigid-jointed structures
Design, model and calculate a simple industrial structure.
Apply basic design criteria for industrial facilities according to planned operating conditions.
Know and correctly interpret the meaning and scope of current applicable standards and instructions

syllabus_topics: Two-dimensional elements. Slabs, plates and shells

assessment_methods.method: Attendance to laboratory practices and submission of practice reports (P2)

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, students who have completed laboratory practices and submitted reports: a minimum grade of 4/10 is required for both the written exam (P1) and the practice report (P2). If these minimums are met and attendance to practical classes is 85% or higher, the final grade is calculated as 0.75 * P1 + 0.25 * P2. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For students in differentiated evaluation, those who have not performed laboratory practices, or those who have not submitted practice reports, both ordinary and extraordinary evaluations require a minimum grade of 4/10 for the written exam (P1) and a practice exam (P2) assessing laboratory practice knowledge and software use. The final grade is calculated as 0.75 * P1 + 0.25 * P2 if minimums are met; otherwise, it is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For extraordinary evaluation, the attendance to practices and submission of practice reports from the semester are validated.
